frontmatter.title: Hedge Fund Investor Questionnaire Reviewer Checklist
frontmatter.description: A section-by-section review checklist for a hedge fund investor questionnaire for a Delaware limited partnership relying on Section 3(c)(1).
frontmatter.coverage: U.S. hedge fund investor questionnaire for a fully funded, open-end fund, read with its subscription agreement and limited partnership agreement. Not a closed-end drawdown fund such as a private equity fund

sections.label: Investment manager outside the United States

requirements.requirementLabel: Qualified-client dollar thresholds taken from the most recent Commission order
requirements.requirementGuidance: If the fund charges a performance fee, the questionnaire must establish that each investor charged it is a qualified client under a Rule 205-3 route, using for the assets-under-management and net-worth tests the amounts in the Commission's most recent order, unless the manager is neither registered nor required to be registered with the Commission, such as an exempt reporting adviser (a state-registered manager should check its state's rule). Confirm it states those amounts and the order's date, and excludes the primary residence from a natural person's net worth. Practice Guide (Who can be charged a performance fee) Examples:

sources.title: 17 CFR 275.205-3(d)(1)(i): Qualified client by assets under management
sources.proposition: Rule 205-3(d)(1)(i) defines a qualified client to include a person with at least the dollar amount in the most recent order under the adviser's management immediately after entering the contract.
sources.verbatimQuote: (1) The term qualified client means: (i) A natural person who, or a company that, immediately after entering into the contract has, under the management of the investment adviser, at least the applicable dollar amount specified in the most recent order; (ii) A natural person who, or a company that, the investment adviser entering into the contract (and any person acting on his behalf) reasonably believes, immediately prior to entering into the contract, either:

sources.title: SEC Order IA-6961: 2026 qualified-client dollar thresholds
sources.citation: Order Approving Adjustment for Inflation of the Dollar Amount Tests in Rule 205-3 Under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, Advisers Act Release No. IA-6961, § IV (Apr. 28, 2026).
sources.proposition: SEC Order IA-6961 sets the qualified-client assets-under-management threshold at $1,400,000 and the net-worth threshold at more than $2,700,000 for contracts it governs.
sources.verbatimQuote: IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that, for purposes of rule 205-3(d)(1)(i) under the Advisers Act [17 CFR 275.205-3(d)(1)], a qualified client means a natural person who, or a company that, immediately after entering into the contract has at least $1,400,000 under the management of the investment adviser; and IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that, for purposes of rule 205-3(d)(1)(ii)(A) under the Advisers Act [17 CFR 275.205-3(d)(1)(ii)(A)], a qualified client means a natural person who, or a company that, the investment adviser entering into the contract (and any person acting on his behalf) reasonably believes, immediately prior to entering into the contract, has a net worth (together, in the case of a natural person, with assets held jointly with a spouse) of more than $2,700,000.

sources.title: 17 CFR 275.205-3(d)(1)(ii)(A): Net-worth test
sources.proposition: Rule 205-3(d)(1)(ii)(A) sets the qualified-client net-worth test and excludes the primary residence from a natural person's assets.
sources.verbatimQuote: (ii) A natural person who, or a company that, the investment adviser entering into the contract (and any person acting on his behalf) reasonably believes, immediately prior to entering into the contract, either: (A) Has a net worth (together, in the case of a natural person, with assets held jointly with a spouse) of more than the applicable dollar amount specified in the most recent order. requirements.requirementLabel: Pooled investors: each equity owner bearing the allocation tested
requirements.requirementGuidance: Where an investor is a private investment company, registered investment company, or business development company, Rule 205-3 treats each equity owner that bears the performance fee as the client, and each must be a qualified client, meaning it meets a Rule 205-3 test such as assets under management or net worth, unless the manager is neither registered nor required to be registered with the Commission, such as an exempt reporting adviser (a state-registered manager should check its state's rule). Confirm the questionnaire identifies that investor and collects its owners' status. Practice Guide (Who can be charged a performance fee) Examples:

sources.title: 17 CFR 275.205-3(b): Identification of the client
sources.proposition: Rule 205-3(b) treats each equity owner of a private investment company, registered investment company, or business development company that is charged gain-based compensation as a client.

requirements.requirementLabel: Section 3(c)(7) fund: qualified-purchaser status at acquisition
requirements.requirementGuidance: A Section 3(c)(7) fund must be owned exclusively by persons who were qualified purchasers when they acquired their interests, apart from holdings Rule 3c-5 excludes, such as a knowledgeable employee's. Confirm the questionnaire asks each investor the qualified-purchaser questions or the facts of a Rule 3c-5 exclusion, and the partnership agreement and memorandum are conformed to the Section 3(c)(7) exclusion. Practice Guide (3(c)(1) and 3(c)(7) funds) Examples:

sources.title: 15 U.S.C. § 80a-3(c)(7)(A): Qualified-purchaser private-fund exclusion
sources.proposition: Section 3(c)(7)(A) excludes an issuer whose outstanding securities are owned exclusively by persons who were qualified purchasers at the time of acquisition and which is not making a public offering.
sources.verbatimQuote: Any issuer, the outstanding securities of which are owned exclusively by persons who, at the time of acquisition of such securities, are qualified purchasers, and which is not making and does not at that time propose to make a public offering of such securities.

sources.title: 17 CFR 270.3c-5(b): Beneficial ownership by knowledgeable employees
sources.proposition: Rule 3c-5(b) excludes securities held by knowledgeable employees, and certain related holders, from the Section 3(c)(1) beneficial-owner count and the Section 3(c)(7) qualified-purchaser ownership test.
sources.verbatimQuote: For purposes of determining the number of beneficial owners of a Section 3(c)(1) Company, and whether the outstanding securities of a Section 3(c)(7) Company are owned exclusively by qualified purchasers, there shall be excluded securities beneficially owned by: (1) A person who at the time such securities were acquired was a Knowledgeable Employee of such Company; (2) A company owned exclusively by Knowledgeable Employees; (3) Any person who acquires securities originally acquired by a Knowledgeable Employee in accordance with this section, provided that such securities were acquired by such person in accordance with § 270.3c-6

requirements.requirementLabel: Section 3(c)(1) beneficial-owner questions for entity investors
requirements.requirementGuidance: In a Section 3(c)(1) fund, confirm the questionnaire asks an entity investor whether it holds 10% or more of the fund's voting securities and whether it is, or but for Section 3(c)(1) or 3(c)(7) would be, an investment company, and, if both, its number of beneficial owners. It may also ask whether the investor was formed to invest in the fund, whether its owners choose individually whether to invest, and whether the investment exceeds 40% of its assets. Practice Guide (Subscription eligibility) Examples:

sources.title: 15 U.S.C. § 80a-3(c)(1): Private-fund exclusion
sources.proposition: Investment Company Act section 3(c)(1) excludes an issuer whose outstanding securities are beneficially owned by not more than one hundred persons and which is not making a public offering.
sources.verbatimQuote: Notwithstanding subsection (a), none of the following persons is an investment company within the meaning of this subchapter: (1) Any issuer whose outstanding securities (other than short-term paper) are beneficially owned by not more than one hundred persons (or, in the case of a qualifying venture capital fund, 250 persons) and which is not making and does not presently propose to make a public offering of its securities.

sources.title: 15 U.S.C. § 80a-3(c)(1)(A): Company-investor look-through
sources.proposition: Section 3(c)(1)(A) counts a company investor as one beneficial owner unless it owns 10 percent or more of the issuer's voting securities and is, or but for section 3(c)(1) or 3(c)(7) would be, an investment company.
sources.verbatimQuote: Beneficial ownership by a company shall be deemed to be beneficial ownership by one person, except that, if the company owns 10 per centum or more of the outstanding voting securities of the issuer, and is or, but for the exception provided for in this paragraph or paragraph (7), would be an investment company, the beneficial ownership shall be deemed to be that of the holders of such company's outstanding securities (other than short-term paper).

requirements.requirementGuidance: Confirm the questionnaire asks, for the investor and its identified owners and control person, whether any of them is on the Office of Foreign Assets Control's sanctions lists, is in a jurisdiction subject to a special measure under Section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act, is a senior foreign political figure or a family member or close associate of one, or is or banks through a foreign shell bank, with an explanation for any yes. Practice Guide (Subscription compliance information) Examples:

sources.title: Managed Funds Association, Sound Practices for Hedge Fund Managers, Appendix IV, Recommendation 2.3
sources.citation: Managed Funds Association, Sound Practices for Hedge Fund Managers, Appendix IV, Recommendation 2.3 (CFTC-hosted copy)
sources.proposition: MFA's sound practices say a hedge fund manager should not accept investments from persons on the OFAC list, from Section 311 jurisdictions, or from foreign shell banks.
sources.verbatimQuote: A Hedge Fund Manager should not accept any investment from or on behalf of any Investor ( a “Prohibited Investor”) that is: • An individual or entity whose name appears on any lists of prohibited persons and entities as may be mandated by applicable law or regulation, including the List of Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons administered by OFAC14 (“OFAC List”) as such lists may be amended from time to time; • An individual or entity who is from a country or territory prohibited by the OFAC sanctions programs; • Resident in, or organized or chartered under the laws of, a jurisdiction that has been designated by the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Treasury under Section 311 of the PATRIOT Act as warranting special measures due to money-laundering concerns; or • A “Prohibited Foreign Shell Bank” (see below).

sources.title: Managed Funds Association, Sound Practices for Hedge Fund Managers, Appendix IV, Recommendation 2.2
sources.citation: Managed Funds Association, Sound Practices for Hedge Fund Managers, Appendix IV, Recommendation 2.2 (CFTC-hosted copy)
sources.proposition: MFA's sound practices say hedge fund subscription agreements should include representations on the investor's status as a prohibited investor or a senior foreign political figure or politically exposed person.
sources.verbatimQuote: Appropriate Identity Provisions Included in Subscription Documents. Fund subscription documents should generally require an Investor to: • Represent and covenant that all evidence of identity provided is genuine and all related information furnished is accurate; 18 | Appendix IV • Agree to provide any information deemed necessary by the Hedge Fund Manager to comply with its AML responsibilities and policies; and • In the case of a Direct Investor, represent that it is investing solely as principal and not for the benefit of any third parties.12 Investor Representations. Hedge Fund subscription agreements should contain a general set of representations from the Investor, stating that they are in compliance with various U.S. federal, state, and international laws and regulations, as well as a set of other disclosures relevant to AML and OFAC compliance. The representation should include statements with respect to the legitimacy of the source of funds being invested, the status of the Investor as a Prohibited Investor, or “Senior Foreign Political Figure/Politically Exposed Person” or “SFPF/PEP”, and if the Investor is a fund of funds or an entity that is acting as an agent or nominee, the representation that the Investor has adopted AML procedures. See Recommendation 2.4.

requirements.requirementLabel: Rule 506(d) disqualification questions for a prospective 20% holder
requirements.requirementGuidance: In a Rule 506 offering, a beneficial owner of 20% or more of the fund's outstanding voting equity securities, calculated on the basis of voting power, is a covered person, and relying on Rule 506(d)'s reasonable-care exception requires factual inquiry in light of the circumstances. Confirm the questionnaire identifies any person that will hold 20% or more, directly or through an investor, with its ownership chain and percentage, and asks about disqualifying events and their dates. Examples:

sources.title: 17 CFR 230.506(d)(1): Bad-actor disqualification
sources.proposition: Rule 506(d)(1) makes the exemption unavailable if a covered person, including a beneficial owner of 20% or more of the issuer's outstanding voting equity securities calculated on the basis of voting power, has a disqualifying event.
sources.verbatimQuote: No exemption under this section shall be available for a sale of securities if the issuer; any predecessor of the issuer; any affiliated issuer; any director, executive officer, other officer participating in the offering, general partner or managing member of the issuer; any beneficial owner of 20% or more of the issuer's outstanding voting equity securities, calculated on the basis of voting power; any promoter connected with the issuer in any capacity at the time of such sale; any investment manager of an issuer that is a pooled investment fund; any person that has been or will be paid (directly or indirectly) remuneration for solicitation of purchasers in connection with such sale of securities; any general partner or managing member of any such investment manager or solicitor; or any director, executive officer or other officer participating in the offering of any such investment manager or solicitor or general partner or managing member of such investment manager or solicitor:

sources.title: 17 CFR 230.506(d)(2)(iv) and instruction: Reasonable care
sources.citation: 17 C.F.R. § 230.506(d)(2)(iv), instruction.
sources.proposition: The reasonable-care exception to Rule 506(d) requires the issuer to have made factual inquiry into whether disqualifications exist.
sources.verbatimQuote: An issuer will not be able to establish that it has exercised reasonable care unless it has made, in light of the circumstances, factual inquiry into whether any disqualifications exist.

(i)The Subscriber is not subject to any conviction, order, judgment, decree, suspension, expulsion, bar, injunction, investigation or proceeding, and has not filed or been named in a registration statement or Regulation A offering statement, such that the Fund (i) would be unable to rely on Rule 506 of Regulation D under the Securities Act or (ii) would be required to make disclosures under Rule 506(d) of Regulation D under the Securities Act, in each case assuming the Subscriber were to own, directly or indirectly, 7 through any contract, arrangement, understanding, relationship or otherwise, twenty percent (20%) or more of the outstanding voting equity securities of the Fund, calculated on the basis of (1) voting power, which includes the power to vote, or to direct the voting of, such securities; and/or (2) investment power, which includes the power to dispose, or to direct the disposition of, such securities.

requirements.requirementLabel: IPO eligibility: FINRA Rule 5130 and 5131 questions
requirements.requirementGuidance: If the fund may buy shares in IPOs (FINRA Rules 5130 and 5131), confirm the questionnaire asks whether the investor or anyone with a beneficial interest in it is a Rule 5130 restricted person, with the facts that decide material support, the share those persons hold, and exempt-account status; whether any of them is an executive officer or director of a public or covered non-public company, or materially supported by one, and which companies; and that the fund's procedures keep answers current for the broker-dealer representations Rules 5130 and 5131 tie to the twelve months before each sale. Examples:

sources.title: FINRA Rule 5130(a)(1): Restrictions on the purchase and sale of initial equity public offerings
sources.citation: FINRA Rule 5130(a)(1).
sources.proposition: FINRA Rule 5130 generally prohibits a member from selling a new issue to an account in which a restricted person has a beneficial interest, subject to the rule's exceptions.
sources.verbatimQuote: A member or a person associated with a member may not sell, or cause to be sold, a new issue to any account in which a restricted person has a beneficial interest, except as otherwise permitted herein.

sources.title: FINRA Rule 5130(i)(8): Material support
sources.citation: FINRA Rule 5130(i)(8).
sources.proposition: FINRA Rule 5130 defines material support as providing more than 25% of a person's income in the prior calendar year and deems immediate family members living in the same household to support each other.
sources.verbatimQuote: "Material support" means directly or indirectly providing more than 25% of a person's income in the prior calendar year. Members of the immediate family living in the same household are deemed to be providing each other with material support.

sources.title: FINRA Rule 5130(b): Preconditions for sale
sources.citation: FINRA Rule 5130(b).
sources.proposition: FINRA Rule 5130(b) requires a member, before selling a new issue to an account, to have obtained in good faith a representation within the prior twelve months.
sources.verbatimQuote: Before selling a new issue to any account, a member must in good faith have obtained within the twelve months prior to such sale, a representation from: (1) Beneficial Owners the account holder(s), or a person authorized to represent the beneficial owners of the account, that the account is eligible to purchase new issues in compliance with this Rule; or (2) Conduits a bank, foreign bank, broker-dealer, or investment adviser or other conduit that all purchases of new issues are in compliance with this Rule.

sources.title: FINRA Rule 5131(b)(1): Spinning
sources.citation: FINRA Rule 5131(b)(1)(A).
sources.proposition: FINRA Rule 5131(b)(1) restricts a member's allocation of new issues to accounts in which an executive officer or director of a public company or covered non-public company, or a person materially supported by one, has a beneficial interest, in the circumstances the rule lists.
sources.verbatimQuote: No member or person associated with a member may allocate shares of a new issue to any account in which an executive officer or director of a public company or a covered non-public company, or a person materially supported by such executive officer or director, has a beneficial interest: (A) if the company is currently an investment banking services client of the member or the member has received compensation from the company for investment banking services in the past 12 months;

sources.title: FINRA Rule 5131(e)(6): Material support
sources.citation: FINRA Rule 5131(e)(6).
sources.proposition: FINRA Rule 5131 defines material support as providing more than 25% of a person's income in the prior calendar year and deems persons living in the same household to support each other.
sources.verbatimQuote: "Material support" means directly or indirectly providing more than 25% of a person's income in the prior calendar year. Persons living in the same household are deemed to be providing each other with material support.

sources.title: FINRA Rule 5131, Supplementary Material .02(a): Annual representation
sources.citation: FINRA Rule 5131, Supplementary Material .02(a).
sources.proposition: For Rule 5131(b), a member may rely on a written representation obtained within the prior 12 months from an account's beneficial owners about executive-officer, director and material-support status and the companies involved.
sources.verbatimQuote: For the purposes of Rule 5131(b), a member may rely upon a written representation obtained within the prior 12 months from the beneficial owner(s) of the account, or a person authorized to represent the beneficial owner(s) of the account, as to whether such beneficial owner(s) is an executive officer or director or person materially supported by an executive officer or director and if so, the company(ies) on whose behalf such executive officer or director serves.

requirements.requirementLabel: Manager outside the United States: questions reflect its adviser status
requirements.requirementGuidance: If the investment manager's principal office and place of business is outside the United States, the questionnaire should reflect its Investment Advisers Act status, as registered, exempt as a non-U.S. private fund adviser, or a foreign private adviser, and its home-country requirements. The Hedge Fund Investor Questionnaire (Manager Outside the U.S.) makes these changes. Practice Guide (Manager outside the United States) Examples:

sources.title: 17 CFR 275.203(m)-1(b): Non-United States private fund advisers
sources.proposition: Rule 203(m)-1(b) exempts an adviser with its principal office outside the United States whose only U.S.-person clients are qualifying private funds and whose U.S.-managed assets are private fund assets of less than $150 million.
sources.verbatimQuote: (b) Non-United States investment advisers. For purposes of section 203(m) of the Act (15 U.S.C. 80b-3(m)), an investment adviser with its principal office and place of business outside of the United States is exempt from the requirement to register under section 203 of the Act if: (1) The investment adviser has no client that is a United States person except for one or more qualifying private funds; and (2) All assets managed by the investment adviser at a place of business in the United States are solely attributable to private fund assets, the total value of which is less than $150 million.

sources.title: Investment Advisers Act of 1940 § 202(a)(30), 15 U.S.C. § 80b-2(a)(30)
sources.proposition: Section 202(a)(30) defines a foreign private adviser by the absence of a U.S. place of business, fewer than 15 U.S. clients and private fund investors, and less than $25 million attributable to them, among other conditions.
sources.verbatimQuote: The term "foreign private adviser" means any investment adviser who- (A) has no place of business in the United States; (B) has, in total, fewer than 15 clients and investors in the United States in private funds advised by the investment adviser; (C) has aggregate assets under management attributable to clients in the United States and investors in the United States in private funds advised by the investment adviser of less than $25,000,000, or such higher amount as the Commission may, by rule, deem appropriate in accordance with the purposes of this subchapter; and

sources.verbatimQuote: Our other investment adviser subsidiaries (“Non-US Adviser Subsidiaries”), to the extent they act as investment advisers within the meaning of the Advisers Act, are exempt from registration thereunder by virtue of, among other things, the foreign private adviser exemption set forth in Sections 202(a)(30) and 203(b)(3) of the Advisers Act and Rule 202(a)(30)-1 thereunder.
